key_insight: Convert noisy inpainting supervision into a clean editing objective via a self-bootstrapping loop: use inpainting outputs to create pseudo paired data, then train an editor that focuses on lip motion while preserving full visual context.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of perfect training pairs for audio-driven visual dubbing, which forces prior methods to hallucinate missing context and causes visual artifacts and identity drift.
method: Stage an initial inpainting-based model to produce pseudo paired examples where only lip motion changes while context is incomplete.
Train a context-aware editing model to modify the lip region conditioned on audio and full-frame context, emphasizing identity and temporal consistency.
Iteratively refine the pseudo-dataset and editor (self-bootstrapping), using the editor's outputs as improved supervision to break the hallucination loop.
impact: Provides a practical recipe to move from artifact-prone inpainting to robust, identity-preserving lip edits without requiring perfect paired data, making visual dubbing more reliable for research and production.
